impact_scope.description: S1 introduces the public ares_queue_wait_empty(channel, timeout_ms) API for waiting until a channel query queue becomes empty or a timeout expires.

evidence: S0 has no matching public declaration for ares_queue_wait_empty in the selected production files.
Because this anchored callable did not exist in S0, H0 had no obligation to invoke or expose it.
S1 declares CARES_EXTERN ares_status_t ares_queue_wait_empty(ares_channel_t *channel, int timeout_ms) in include/ares.h.
H0 invokes DNS reply parsers and ares_create_query only; it does not initialize a channel and call ares_queue_wait_empty or supply its timeout argument.
The API exposes caller-visible outcomes for unsupported threading, invalid channels, expiration, and an empty queue, none of which H0 reaches through its existing entrypoints.

new_harness_obligation.description: H0 must add a call to the new public entry point, supply an initialized channel and timeout value, and construct relevant queue states to expose its wait, timeout, and empty-queue behavior.
evidence: Calling ares_queue_wait_empty is a new harness action that was impossible and unnecessary in S0.
Its channel and timeout_ms parameters require caller-controlled setup not supplied automatically by any existing H0 call.

reason: The identity-anchored public callable is absent in S0 and introduced in S1. Therefore the same-scope gap changes from false to true. Exercising it requires a concrete new harness call and caller-supplied channel/timeout state, so the default truth table yields NEW and the fixed rule requires maintenance.
